description: Query-executor edge cases whose Snowflake-correct behaviour the engine already implements. A scalar subquery returning more than one row raises the single-row cardinality error. > ALL over a set containing a NULL is UNKNOWN, so no rows qualify. For an OUTER join, a predicate in ON keeps the unmatched left rows where the same predicate in WHERE would drop them. GROUP BY ALL groups by every non-aggregated SELECT column. Grouping and set-operation equality is the DELIBERATE OPPOSITE of predicate three-valued logic: GROUP BY collapses all NULL keys into ONE group and UNION treats NULLs as EQUAL when de-duplicating, while the predicate side (where NULL = NULL is UNKNOWN) lives in query-null-three-valued-logic. Aggregates over an EMPTY table answer one row where COUNT is 0 but SUM, MIN and MAX are NULL, not zero. GROUP BY <n> and ORDER BY <n> are 1-based positional references. And a self-join under two aliases must resolve each alias to its own side, so m.name is the matched manager's name and not the employee's own. Converted 1:1 from query/QueryExecutorEdgeCaseTest (now retired); the Java asserted row COUNTS almost throughout, so the converted tests pin which rows.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE emp (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
SELECT name, (SELECT name FROM departments) FROM emp WHERE id = 1
SELECT sal FROM emp WHERE sal > ALL (SELECT s FROM t)
CREATE TABLE emp (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE d (dept VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)
SELECT e.id FROM emp e LEFT JOIN d ON e.dept = d.dept AND d.region = 'EU'
SELECT e.id FROM emp e LEFT JOIN d ON e.dept = d.dept WHERE d.region = 'EU'
CREATE TABLE t (dept VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)
SELECT dept, region, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY ALL
SELECT k, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY k
SELECT v FROM t1 UNION SELECT v FROM t2
SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(v), MIN(v), MAX(v) FROM t
CREATE TABLE t (dept VARCHAR, amt INTEGER)
SELECT dept, SUM(amt) FROM t GROUP BY 1
CREATE TABLE t (name VARCHAR, sal INTEGER)
SELECT name, sal FROM t ORDER BY 2 DESC
CREATE TABLE emp (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, mgr_id INTEGER)
SELECT e.name, m.name FROM emp e JOIN emp m ON e.mgr_id = m.id
